help.stock: Stock details are optional. Add a stock name, supplier, received date, or stock expenses only when you need a fuller purchasing record.
help.products: Think of products as Group → Variety → Item. Example: iPhone 15 Pro Max → Silver 256 GB → each phone's IMEI. Start with the group, then record the exact variety you received.
help.catalog: A product group keeps the same main product together. Each variety is one version inside that group, and individual items can carry their own identifiers.
help.record: Enter how many units you received and the buying price per unit. For individually tracked stock, add each item's IMEI, serial number, or other identifier.
help.review: Check the products you recorded, then save a draft or finish and receive the stock. Optional stock details are included only when you entered them.
help.familyAssignment: A product group keeps related versions of the same product together. Example: iPhone 15 Pro Max is the group; Silver 256 GB and Black 512 GB are varieties inside it.
help.autoSku: A variety is one exact version inside a product group, for example Silver · 256 GB. Tunakuza handles the SKU automatically.
help.existingSku: A variety is one exact version inside a product group. Choose an existing variety if it is already there, or add a new one.
help.existingCategory: Choose a product group, then choose an existing variety or add a new one inside it.
help.newCategory: A product group is the main product people recognize, for example iPhone 15 Pro Max. After creating the group, add its first variety.
help.uncategorized: Use a simple product when you do not need a product group. You can still record it by quantity or track each item separately.
